findings.title: Settled/unsettled cash split misattributes a sale's fee to settled cash instead of the unsettled proceeds it came from
findings.observed: Sold 7 XLV for gross proceeds $1,101.10 with a $0.03 SEC/TAF fee (net cash to me: $1,101.07, matching my own fill record). /portfolio's cash tiles after this fill: CASH $5,553.31, '$4,452.21 settled - $1,101.10 unsettled'. Settled dropped by exactly $0.03 (from the prior session's $4,452.24) even though the fee was charged against this sale's own unsettled proceeds, and unsettled shows the gross $1,101.10 rather than the net $1,101.07. The total ($5,553.31) is correct; only the split is off, by $0.03 in opposite directions. The harness's own independently-tracked paper-broker book agrees with the correct split: settled_cash 4452.24 (unchanged), the $0.03 fee absorbed inside the new unsettled bucket.
findings.expected: A regulatory fee on a sale should reduce the unsettled proceeds that sale produced, not the already-settled cash sitting untouched from before it.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a small dollar amount but the wrong bucket: it understates settled (redeployable) cash and overstates unsettled cash by the same amount every time a sale carries a fee. On a book with many small trades this compounds into a settled-cash figure I can no longer trust to the cent -- exactly the kind of provenance gap the mandate cares about.
repro: Sell a position that incurs a SEC/TAF fee
Open /portfolio and read the CASH tile's settled/unsettled breakdown
Compare against the fill's own gross proceeds and fee: settled is short by the fee amount, unsettled is not
